summary: Build humanitarian supply chain resilience skills in GIS, contingency stocks, MEAL, and crisis logistics. Explore the practical five-day course.
lede: Resilient Humanitarian Supply Chains and Logistics Intelligence helps humanitarian teams anticipate disruption, maintain critical relief flows, and recover operations when conflict, disease outbreaks, floods, droughts, weak infrastructure, or access changes affect plans. You will connect ISO 31000 risk principles, the Core Humanitarian Standard, GIS, and MEAL evidence to decisions about suppliers, routes, contingency stocks, and accountability. Through structured exercises, you will practise hazard and access mapping, commodity classification, transport and lead-time scenarios, stock triggers, supplier segmentation, route visibility, indicator design, and donor reporting. You will develop practical outputs including a disruption risk register, GIS-based access map, continuity scorecard, resilience plan, contingency stock strategy, digital visibility dashboard concept, and MEAL-linked reporting structure.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who connect humanitarian procurement, logistics execution, programme performance, and crisis decision-making. It suits intermediate practitioners who already work with operational plans or field data and need a structured approach to humanitarian supply chain resilience.
modules: ISO 31000 Risk and GIS Exposure Mapping
Digital Logistics Visibility and Data Quality
prerequisites: You should have working experience in humanitarian logistics, emergency procurement, programme operations, disaster management, GIS, or MEAL. No coding or advanced statistics are required. Familiarity with spreadsheets and routine operational reporting will help you complete the exercises, while GIS and digital data activities use guided templates rather than production-system configuration.
